bibl.author: atiśa dīpaṃkaraśrījñāna

bibl.title: rgyal sras bslab pa kun las btus pa'i legs par bshad pa
རྒྱལ་སྲས་བསླབ་པ་ཀུན་ལས་བཏུས་པའི་ལེགས་པར་བཤད་པ
bibl.author: sems dpa' chen po gzhon nu rgyal mchog
bibl.note:
According to the colophon, notes (zin bris) based on the sayings (gsung sgros) of the monk brTson 'grus seng ge that were composed as a memorandum (brjed byang) on an instruction (man ngag) pertaining to the meaning of the 28 verses of the base text and on the author's own understanding.
The author addresses the view of other unidentified scholars.
This work appears first (volume ka) in a collection of the author's works. For the second work (volume kha), see (ID:5394), for the third (volume ga) (ID:5398), for the fourth (volume ca) (ID:5400), for the fifth (volume cha) (ID: 5402), for the sixth (volume ja) (ID: 5404). Five more volume appeared in [KUYBGM7V], vol. 105.

bibl.title: sngon 'gro'i chos zab mo nyams su len tshul
སྔོན་འགྲོའི་ཆོས་ཟབ་མོ་ཉམས་སུ་ལེན་ཚུལ
bibl.author: sems dpa' chen po gzhon nu rgyal mchog
bibl.note: Work presented as a preliminary to Bodhipaṭhapradīpa (ID:3722). It mainly discusses Atiśa (ID:3745)'s life and the history surrounding him and his teachings in Tibet, providing some interesting historical details.

bibl.title: sngon 'gro'i chos dge ba'i bshes gnyen bsten tshul sogs

bibl.author: sems dpa' chen po gzhon nu rgyal mchog
bibl.note: This text is presented as a prelimanary to the Bodhipaṭhapradīpa (ID:3744). It mainly discusses Atiśa's life and the history surrounding him and his teachings in Tibet.

bibl.title: byang chub lam gyi sgron ma las sangs rgyas kyi bstan pa la 'jug pa'i rim pa dal 'byor rnyed dka' dang mi rtag pa'i chos bsam tshul zab mo

bibl.author: sems dpa' chen po gzhon nu rgyal mchog

bibl.title: dal 'byor rnyed dka' ba bsam pa'i tshul zab mo
དལ་འབྱོར་རྙེད་དཀའ་བ་བསམ་པའི་ཚུལ་ཟབ་མོ
bibl.author: sems dpa' chen po gzhon nu rgyal mchog
bibl.note: Text in three parts, dealing with the portion of the Bodhipathapradīpa (ID:3744) on the difficulty to attain a human rebirth. Numerous references to the lineages of 'Brom ston (ID:3827), Po to ba (ID:3829) etc., to their works and Indian texts (not for contesting views).
